title: Lifetimes with Slices and Views
goal: Understand how functions return slices of input data without allocating new memory.

sections.text: Parsing strings or binary protocols in Rust usually returns slices of the input. You return views into existing memory instead of allocating new buffers.

sections.caption: Single input reference: elision ties output to input.

sections.text: Lifetime elision automatically connects the returned slice to the single input parameter. No lifetime annotations are needed when there is only one input reference.
When a function takes two references but only returns a view into one, default elision fails with `E0106`. You must explicitly name the lifetime of the input that is sliced.

sections.caption: data has lifetime 'a, prefix is unlinked.

sections.text: Unlinking `prefix` allows the caller to mutate or drop the prefix variable immediately after the call. The returned slice only borrows `data`.

explanation: Understand how functions return slices of input data without allocating new memory.
